{{Quote|It's all the rage. Experience shows us that losing by the narrowest possible margin until almost the end is often the way to win a lengthy war.|Turman Durra to Voyce Evlen|<ref name="MK">''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]''</ref>}}
'''Virtual sabacc''', or '''Excess''', was a mental variant of the card game [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]]. Players imagined and dealt hands of cards mentally rather than using physical decks, giving them the chance to potentially cheat by mentally manipulating their cards. However, the game's objective was not simply to obtain the best hand, as players had to choose a winning hand that was not unbeatable. In a lengthy series of hands, the player who lost by the narrowest cumulative margin could win the game.<ref name="MK" />

In [[44 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]'' to [[44 ABY]].</ref> [[Turman Durra]], a member of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] [[Commando/Legends|commando]] unit [[Wraith Squadron]], offered to play virtual sabacc with [[Galactic Alliance Defense Fleet|Alliance Navy]] [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Voyce Evlen]] while they waited for Alliance [[Galactic Alliance Army|Army]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Stavin Thaal]] to arrive at their rendezvous. Durra explained the rules and compared the game's strategy to warfare, noting that losing by the narrowest possible margin until near the end could be a means of ultimately winning a lengthy conflict.<ref name="MK" />
